80401.subject: AI Ambition Is Cheap;Why Isolated AI Tools Break at Enterprise Scale; Most companies don’t have an AI agent problem. They have an architecture problem
80401.body:
AI Frontier

Автор: Steve Nouri


Автор: Steve Nouri

    
    
    Прочитайте цю статтю на LinkedIn, щоб приєднатися до обговорення

Generative and agentic AI have made experimentation easier than ever, but launching pilots is not the same as creating business value. The real divide is now between companies that test AI and companies that can repeatedly build, deploy, adopt, and scale it. Most wining companies that I talked with concentrated their transformation on three or fewer priority areas. They did not spread AI across the organization. They focused resources where the economic impact was highest. That is the first lesson: stop collecting use cases. Many companies deploy copilots, agents, and automation tools inside existing processes. This may improve individual tasks, but it rarely changes the economics of the business. The larger opportunity is to redesign complete workflows. Instead of asking how AI can accelerate one step in claims processing, supply-chain planning, customer support, or software development, leaders should ask what the entire process would look like if it were rebuilt around AI. McKinsey found that reimagining workflows end to end had one of the strongest correlations with value. The second lesson is that AI transformation is a people transformation. Agents may take over routine execution, coordination, and some decision-making, but this changes human roles rather than removing the need for strong teams. Companies must redesign responsibilities, retrain employees, and combine human judgment with machine execution. The third lesson is speed. DBS once needed 18 months to put its first AI model into production. It can now deploy one every two months. The advantage is not any single model. It is the organizational system that allows the company to keep moving faster. Finally, AI cannot be delegated to the technology department. Successful transformation requires the CEO to make it a top priority, while business leaders, finance, HR, product, and technology teams share responsibility for delivery. AI becomes valuable when the business owns the outcome, not when IT owns another project. The companies winning with AI are not necessarily using the most advanced models. They are choosing fewer priorities, redesigning complete workflows, preparing people for adoption, and building the ability to move from idea to impact repeatedly. AI ambition gets attention.
